# Exact interval superlevels for monotone line weights, and the concavity caveat

This is a bounded arithmetic lemma for the anchored shell-plus-atomic coefficient. It does not prove the corresponding superlevel claim for general concave radius profiles in higher integer rank.

## 1. The maximal-core root really is concave

Let C be a compact convex source, J a full-dimensional centered convex body containing zero in its interior, and a(z) an affine center map that lies in the real fiber K_z throughout a convex base domain. Define

    r(z)=max{t>=0:a(z)+tJ subset K_z}.

The maximum is attained: the admissible scales form a nonempty closed bounded subset of [0,infinity), with boundedness following from any ball contained in J and boundedness of C. Convexity gives

    a((1-s)z+s w)+[(1-s)r(z)+s r(w)]J
      =(1-s)(a(z)+r(z)J)+s(a(w)+r(w)J)
      subset K_((1-s)z+s w).

Thus r is concave. An arbitrary selection of smaller contained copies need not have this property. This distinction must be retained when studying an anchorwise coefficient.

## 2. Exact monotone line formula

For nonnegative weights w_0>=w_1>=...>=w_N on the consecutive integer bases 0,...,N, extend weights by zero outside this interval. Put

    S_j=sum_(i=0)^j w_i, S_(-1)=0,
    D_j=min(S_j,S_N-S_(j-1)),
    R_j=sum_(h>=1) min(w_(j-h),w_(j+h)),
    F_j=D_j+R_j.

These are exactly the closed weighted atomic depth, equal reflected-copy coefficient, and combined shell coefficient at the integer anchor j. Monotonicity gives the exact identity

    R_j=S_min(2j,N)-S_j,
    F_j=min(A_j,B_j),
    A_j=S_min(2j,N),
    B_j=S_N-S_(j-1)+S_min(2j,N)-S_j.                 (1)

A_j is nondecreasing. Using the zero extension for the last two terms,

    B_(j+1)-B_j=-w_j-w_(j+1)+w_(2j+1)+w_(2j+2)<=0. (2)

Both comparisons of terms in (2) follow from their ordered indices and monotonicity. Therefore every superlevel {j:F_j>=c} is an integer interval, possibly empty. The same holds for nondecreasing weights by reversing the indexing. No concavity of w itself or differentiability is needed.

This gives an actual finite intersection lemma: for any finite collection of monotone weight profiles on the same consecutive base, their coefficient superlevels are integer intervals. If every two of these intervals intersect, all of them have one common integer anchor. Indeed their maximum lower endpoint is no greater than their minimum upper endpoint. If all profiles use the same affine actual center graph, their corresponding shell guarantees hold at the same deterministic point of that fiber. This lemma neither adds overlapping cap credits nor asserts that its intersection hypothesis holds automatically.

## 3. Arbitrary positive retained weights do not have interval superlevels

Even in one integer dimension, positivity of every retained core is insufficient. Take the complete base {0,...,8}, put weight one at 0,1,4,8, and weight epsilon at all five other bases, where 0<epsilon<1/3. Direct finite sums give

    (D_2,R_2,F_2)=(2+epsilon,1+epsilon,3+2epsilon),
    (D_3,R_3,F_3)=(2+2epsilon,3epsilon,2+5epsilon),
    (D_4,R_4,F_4)=(2+3epsilon,1+3epsilon,3+6epsilon).

The weights at 2 and 4 have the same integer parity, but

    F_3<min(F_2,F_4).

For example epsilon=1/100 gives coefficients 151/50, 41/20, 153/50. Any level strictly between 41/20 and 151/50 has a non-midpoint-closed superlevel trace.

These are actual contained homothetic cores: take C=[0,8] times J with |J|=1 and retain radii w_j^(1/d) at the common center zero. All original fibers are full-dimensional and equal to J. The selected roots are not concave, and the maximal roots are instead identically one. Therefore this counterexample does not refute the stronger question restricted to maximal cores or arbitrary concave radius roofs.

## 4. Remaining scope

Exact-sign searches of piecewise-affine positive concave roofs on small complete planar lattice polytopes found no counterexample to midpoint-superlevel convexity of D+R, including several powers w=r^d. Such a search is not used in any theorem above and establishes no higher-rank convexity. The proved content is the maximal-root concavity, the explicit monotone-line formula and finite interval intersection lemma, and the exact nonconcave retained-weight obstruction.
